We have had no opportunity to find our own objective opinions to contradict whatever it might be that the Prosecution may put forward. The Prosecution has nowhere denied that it has untimely provided disclosure of evidence to us at this point. In the sake of brevity and to be expeditious for this Tribunal, I just want to say that, based on all of the written claims that we have in our motion for adjournment and our supplementary motion for adjournment, based upon all the worthy arguments of Madam Residovic and Mr. Karabdic, the attorney for Mr. Delic, we further show that there is no way that in the interests of fairness, as this Tribunal is set up, that we could possibly be prepared for defence of any of the accused before four months. We ask that this case be adjourned and continued until May 20th. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. McMurrey. I think we will turn to the other motions which were filed ‑‑‑‑

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Can I respond to Mr. Ostberg, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You can, Mr. Karabdic. Yes, you can respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: I support fully the arguments of Ms. McMurrey and of Mr. Brackovic. I will not repeat their argument. Allow me just to comment briefly on the statement of the Prosecution. He said that I received the indictment on 18th June or thereabouts, June 1996. It is correct that I received the indictment at that time, but I immediately said and took appropriate action, I saw that this was an indictment that had been composed in an irregular fashion and I did everything I could to regularise it. I think that the Appeals Chamber, the Bench, the Appeals Bench, actually said that I was right in many aspects, because they stated that all the irregularities or defects in the indictment exist both in the factual and the legal aspects. In the ruling of the Appeals Bench, they stated that the Prosecutor should as soon as possible clarify certain issues and to improve or to solve the contradictory alternatives in the indictment. But this has not been done. When I took all those measures, trying to have this solved, I expected that the indictment would be corrected and that then I would be able to prepare myself for one line of accusations. As it is now, since the indictment has remained in force, I have to prepare my defence for several alternatives which, as the Appeals Bench has stated themselves, are contradictory. It does take a lot of time. I have to determine myself what the provisions are that my client can use in his defence and this takes a lot of time. This is the reason why I have asked for an adjournment. I find myself in a situation in which no Defence counsel has had to find themselves. I do not know what are the provisions according to which my client has been charged and what the provisions are according to which he can offer his defence. I did not say that the attitude of the Prosecution was hostile. I can state that I have co‑operated very well with the Prosecution. The fact is that we did not get the addresses of the witnesses with the statements that we have received. We do not know where to locate the witnesses. In this way the Prosecution has made it impossible for us to do it. In order to be able to find out their addresses and in order to be able to exercise our right to examine the witnesses, we need so much time for that. This is the reason for the adjournment. I still am of the opinion that what the Prosecution has disclosed to us, this notice of expert witnesses, does not fulfil their obligation, according to the Statute, to disclose the evidence and to provide us with the statement of the expert witnesses. This is indefinite, unclear, so that it is of no use to us. This is my impression after the brief time that I had to study it from yesterday until today. The Prosecutor has to have some other material on the basis of which he knows that these expert witnesses could testify. I want to see that. Please, show it to us. This is not satisfactory, that we are given such indefinite and unclear information. This cannot be a basis for the defence, because it does not contain any specific, detailed circumstances or information about what the witnesses would talk about, except for the general view of the Prosecution that they will talk about the general conditions, general circumstances. This is not something that we can accept. The things that happened in Bosnia and the fact that a state was established in conditions such as those and that the state came under attack and that it defended itself, not only was the state attacked but the people themselves. This is something you have to bear in mind. This has to be the general assumption behind this whole case. We were all sentenced to death, to extinction. We were assaulted by the fourth strongest force in Europe.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That has nothing to do with the adjournment. It has nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, I apologise, your Honour, this is just something, I say that this issue cannot be avoided in the expert witnesses' testimony. The Prosecution imposes this in the notice. This is not something that you can avoid. You cannot say that this happened in an abstract country regardless of the concrete circumstances. The state was established. It came under attack. You all know what happened. This is the context in which this has to be considered. You cannot just view this one separate case and treat it separate from the general context. I apologise. I would like to conclude. I still am of the view that the trial should be adjourned for four months, as I said earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have some other motions standing in the name of Landzo. Can we here your comments on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may address the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let us see how you get into it at all, because it stands by your first application under Rule 73.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I was going to suggest that maybe we take the motion for enlargement of time to file additional motions first, because that might be the most expeditious way to move along. We are asking for leave of the Court to file additional motions. I believe there was a 60‑day time period that passed. The reason that we need additional time to file additional pretrial motions now is that, based on the disclosure of the Prosecution which has only recently occurred, it is only then after reviewing the evidence against us that we can maybe formulate what pretrial motions need to be filed in response to the evidence that has been given to us. So it is only now at the time that we are still continuing to get disclosure of evidence that we may have an opportunity to come up with new issues that are arising as the evidence is disclosed.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are prepared to enlarge the time for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are prepared to enlarge the time for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then should I go to the ‑‑ should I choose the order, your Honours, or should you?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Well, I suppose you can, but my fear is whether you could not look at Rule 73 itself and see how you come in, and see whether all the motions which you have intended to move here come within the provisions of Rule 73.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I was asking for a waiver, I suppose, under Rule 73 to continue to file pretrial motions as they become necessary, because I believe that Rule 73 must have assumed that within a short period of time after indictment disclosure would have been provided to the Defence, but because disclosure is now nine, 10 months later ‑‑‑‑

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: This is disclosure within Rule 73.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: No, your Honour, disclosure is not within Rule 73, but as far as applications for the exclusion of evidence, we cannot make that determination on whether evidence should be excluded until we receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Application for severance.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So it is premature at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: It is premature?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: It is premature until we receive the evidence, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You could not move it. So which is the other one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: So the application for the separate trial I believe that ‑‑‑‑

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That has already been decided upon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, it was decided and it was filed timely, earlier. It was filed within the Statute.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: This is not an Appeals Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: No. We are asking for reconsideration of that issue at this point.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Under which of the Rules?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Under the request for enlargement of time to ‑‑‑‑

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, it does not enable you to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: OK. I think since we are also unclear, I am unclear, I am asking the Court for clarification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, uou are not quite familiar with what has happened before now or you were not quite familiar with the scope of Rule 73 at the time you drew up your motions. This was your problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am asking the Court to ‑‑‑‑

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The waiver is the waiver of your delay. It is not the waiver of other subject matter which comes within Rule 73.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is not a waiver. It does not waive subject matters because they are specific and prescribed, the matters which come under Rule 73.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am asking you, as the Court just stated that the exclusion of evidence cannot be filed within 60 days of the first appearance of the accused if the Prosecution has not disclosed evidence, so there would have to be a waiver under that one particular issue, would there not?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, that can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: OK. The application for separate trials or severance of crimes joined or for separate trials, that says that it had to be filed within 60 days.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, that has been decided. There is a decision of the Trial Chamber on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: So if there is additional argument on that area and the defendant is asking for reconsideration based on additional argument ‑‑‑‑

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is why I asked you for the Rule enabling you to do that. Then you read that Rule and tell me the circumstances under which you can do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am relying on Rule 73(C) which says that upon a showing of good cause the Trial Chamber may grant relief.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In respect of waiver. Have you not read it carefully? Read it carefully, showing good cause in respect of waiver that you have not waived.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Right. The waiver is that if we did not file the motion within 60 days then we would have waived all right to bring forth that issue to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. Then upon showing good cause we grant the relief in respect of waiver.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes. So you are asking us to show good cause at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In respect of which of the subject matters coming within one, two, three, four, five of 73(A)?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: The only one we have filed that I believe may have been waived, the argument, would be the argument for separate trial. Everything else I believe has not been waived.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But you cannot even raise argument of separate trials which have been decided by the Trial Chamber here, except you are now appealing on that. In fact, you did not appeal on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: It was an improper vehicle to ask for reconsideration and further argument, is that what the Tribunal is saying?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You should understand what errors you have committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: OK. Then we will try to skip the separate trial issue. I believe all the other motions have not been waived.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They do not come within Rule 73. This is what I am telling you. They are not covered by Rule 73. So you come under the wrong Rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I will ask the Court, based on the disclosure of evidence and as the pretrial motions, I am going to title all pretrial motions "pretrial motions", that these would be evidentiary motions to ask for clarification of the Court that really do not fall under 73 at all.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They do not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: No, they do not. So we can proceed without any fear of waiver.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Why?You mean you could proceed without following or observing any Rules?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: No, your Honour. What is my understanding is that the specific issues listed in Rule 73, if they were not raised or they have already been taken care of, that is fine, but the issues, motion for equal access to witnesses, the motion for disclosure of exculpatory evidence and the motion for designation of witnesses and evidence to be used, if those do not fall under 73 and therefore they have never been waived, they are a different breed of pretrial motion that have to be address as they arise prior to the trial of case.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Some of them need no motions at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If you read Rule 66, Rule 67 you will find your rights there. They give you a sufficient showing of what you do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Maybe since they do not need to be titled "pretrial motions" they should just be addressed at the status conference under Rule 5 which would mean non-compliance with the Rules as ordered earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Actually I am only explaining to you that you have come under the wrong Rule and we cannot entertain your applications, full stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is all it means.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: So they are issues that will be brought up informally, not in the form of a motion but can be determined at the status conference?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: OK, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I did not think it was necessary to call on the Prosecution to make any comments because there is nothing new before the Tribunal properly for me to allow you to say anything. Have you anything to say, Ms. McHenry?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your indulgence I would like to say one thing while this is still a public session. I understand we are going to discuss many specific issues later on in the status hearing, but while this is a public session I want to make sure that the Prosecution on behalf of all trial counsel do officially deny that we have given untimely disclosure. There had been a statement that somehow we were conceding that and I want to make it clear during the open session that we are not conceding that. We can discuss the details later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. McHenry. I think we will have to adjourn at this stage and come back at 3.30 for the status conference. Then we will be able to give our rulings on the question of an adjournment. 1.50 p.m. (Luncheon Adjournment)

procedural_notes.text: (The hearing adjourned for a short time)
